penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: A backend integration audit is fundamentally a review-and-recommendation service; each client's stack is unique, so meaningful audits require human (or deep per-customer AI) analysis that can't be fully templatised across customers without significant manual work.

rationale: The buyer is a specific, identifiable person — a solo technical founder or small-team CTO already paying for Stripe, Clerk, and Supabase — which is a real B2B-adjacent ICP with budget. However, the core service (integration audit, starter kit maintenance, or cross-service breakage monitoring) requires per-customer bespoke work for audits or significant ongoing engineering for a monitoring product, both of which are difficult to automate fully with just Claude + forms + Stripe. The deciding factor is operational autonomy: the most valuable version (audit) is a consulting engagement, and the most automatable version (starter kit) is a one-time sale with no recurring pull.
solution_plan: N/A — recommended for drop after penalties. The audit angle requires hands-on per-client analysis; the starter-kit angle is a commodity with no recurring revenue. A monitoring tool that detects cross-service breakage is the most automatable version but requires building and maintaining integrations with multiple third-party APIs — a significant ongoing engineering burden for a solo non-technical operator.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy build gate (score 5, floor is 7). After the requires_human_fulfillment penalty, total drops to 4.2, below the 5.5 validate threshold.
